newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call steady, gilts seen up in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian call steady, gilts seen up in brisk trade.

text.p: Indian call money was quoted in the 0.10-0.25 percent range in early Monday trade in conditions of good liquidity and poor demand, dealers said.
They said little change was expected in call money rates as banks were flush with funds.
"At the moment, it looks like call money rates will remain in the same range, mostly below 1.0 percent, till at least mid-May," said a dealer at a state-run bank.
"The supply of funds is simply too much right now."
Dealers said they expected trade in government securities to be brisk ahead of an auction of 30 billion rupees of 10-year bonds later on Monday.

"The cut-off at the auction should determine whether prices continue firm or there is a slight correction," a dealer at a private bank said. "Quite a few market players are expecting a cut-off yield around 13.0 percent or slightly below."
"If the cut-off is above that, there could be some selling and prices may fall," he said.
The last auction of 10-year bonds was in February at a cut-off yield of 13.65 percent.
